subject.title: [Bug] Race condition in approval-classifier.ts when tokenization exceeds max tokens

question: Does ACP/security ownership have evidence that a supported agent can execute a tool before OpenClaw returns its requestPermission outcome on current main?
rationale: The current OpenClaw path does not expose the reported asynchronous tokenizer, but only dependency inspection or a live protocol trace can rule out an execution-order defect across the client-agent boundary.

options.title: Require protocol proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and request a redacted ACP message trace, exact toolCall payload, agent/version, configured token limit, and evidence of execution before the permission response.

options.title: Confirm protocol safety
options.body: Close only after ACP ownership verifies that the SDK and supported agents serialize tool execution behind requestPermission and a reasonable current-main attempt does not reproduce the bypass.

recommendation.title: Require protocol proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and request a redacted ACP message trace, exact toolCall payload, agent/version, configured token limit, and evidence of execution before the permission response.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the direct ACP permission-hardening work associated with commit 63dcd28.
